mostWorthwhile.text: Separating chromosome sets before forming two cells was most worthwhile: the descriptions distinguish sister-chromatid separation, new nuclei and division of the shared cytoplasm.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the spindle was comparatively thin: the picture shows fibres, but the result does not explain how tubulin and motor proteins help organize or move them.

surprise.text: The genome-copying result explicitly distinguishes replication of all nuclear DNA, including noncoding regions, from making proteins.

arbitrary.text: Combining the enlarged cell body with separated chromosome sets to form two nuclei felt somewhat abstract; the cutaway explanation helps, but the combination itself does not explain nuclear-envelope re-formation.

continue.text: I would continue: the staged division was clear, and the final reference to different gene-expression patterns suggests an interesting next connection, though the later choices became predictable.
